subject: zoology_2
question_text: Name the valves that guard the left and right atrioventricular apertures in man.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.48, VSAQ 63. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Left aperture
steps.why: The left valve has two flaps because the thick left ventricle needs a smaller, stronger opening to hold against high pressure.
common_mistakes: Putting the tricuspid on the left. Bicuspid is the left valve.
Naming semilunar valves. Those guard the arteries, not the apertures.
steps.memory_tip: LAB RAT — Left Atrium Bicuspid, Right Atrium Tricuspid.
steps.margin_note: Two lines, one for each side.
lines: guarded by the bicuspid valve, also called

steps.label: Right aperture
steps.why: Three flaps close the wider right opening, where the pressure from the thinner right ventricle is lower.
common_mistakes: Naming only one valve when two are asked.
steps.memory_tip: Tri- for three flaps on the right.

lines.text: The right aperture is guarded by the tricuspid

insider_note: One mark each, so both sides must be named. Writing 'mitral valve' for the bicuspid is accepted, but name the side it guards.
